options.description: Proposed: follow ordinary custody through the dock distribution network until an Abyss buyer is found. Earlier familiarity with goods and routes helps; a magical tracking power is unnecessary.

Proposed: intersect a later Abyss operation at a protected site, where the thieves have brought the blade as a suspected valuable instrument. They can be wrong about its use; recovery must not itself settle the ancient history.

questions.question: How can the player recover the stolen sabre without making early petty thieves know its final purpose?

description:
Team Abyss later steals the sabre with incomplete understanding; no heist is implemented.

Proposed draft: return to the same ordinary hall after the theft. Its empty sabre supports are more legible than a newly introduced crime scene; the bell, weights and ceramics remain. Staff disagree about whether to close everything or keep the undamaged collections accessible. A missing cargo entry and a reused packing mark could connect the thieves to the established dock trade, but neither should explain the blade’s purpose. Choose the actual evidence with the heist route rather than inventing a complete provenance.
